hagia-sophia: 1,500 years of Byzantine and Ottoman history under one dome. Visitors enter the upper galleries on a separate ticketed route; worshippers enter free.
blue-mosque: The six-minaret Sultan Ahmed Mosque with its blue İznik tiles. Free; closed to visitors during prayer times.
topkapi: Home of the Ottoman sultans for almost 400 years: courtyards, treasury, sacred relics and the Harem, with views over the Bosphorus.
basilica-cistern: A 6th-century underground water palace with 336 columns and the two Medusa heads; evening sessions cost more.
archaeology: Three museums next to Topkapı: the Alexander Sarcophagus, ancient Near East treasures and the Tiled Kiosk.
suleymaniye: Mimar Sinan's masterpiece on the third hill, with a terrace over the Golden Horn. Free; closed to visitors during prayers.
chora: Some of the finest Byzantine mosaics and frescoes in the world, near the land walls. Check visiting hours before you go.
galata-tower: The medieval Genoese tower with a 360° view over the Golden Horn and the Bosphorus; day and night sessions.
dolmabahce: The 19th-century European-style palace on the Bosphorus, with its crystal staircase and giant chandelier.
beylerbeyi: An elegant summer palace on the Asian shore, under the Bosphorus Bridge.
maidens-tower: The little tower on an islet off Üsküdar, reached by boat; a museum and viewpoint.
rumeli-hisari: The fortress Mehmed II built in four months in 1452, on the narrowest point of the Bosphorus.
istanbul-modern: Modern and contemporary Turkish art in a new building on the Karaköy waterfront.
pera-museum: Orientalist paintings, including Osman Hamdi Bey's "The Tortoise Trainer", near İstiklal Avenue.
rahmi-koc: Cars, trains, ships, planes and a submarine on the Golden Horn; a favourite with families.
isfanbul: Istanbul's big theme park in Eyüpsultan: roller coasters, family rides and shows. Formerly called Vialand.
istanbul-aquarium: One of Europe's largest aquariums, at the Aqua Florya mall by the sea. Marmaray to Florya Akvaryum station.
sea-life: Underwater tunnel with sharks and rays at Forum İstanbul mall; combo tickets with LEGOLAND.
legoland: Indoor LEGO play centre for children aged about 3–10, at Forum İstanbul; cheaper online.
madame-tussauds: Wax figures of Turkish and world celebrities, on İstiklal Avenue.
miniaturk: Open-air park with scale models of famous buildings from Turkey and the Ottoman lands, on the Golden Horn.
whirling-dervishes: An hour-long Sema ceremony in a restored 15th-century hammam in Sirkeci; evening sessions.
city-ferry: The cheapest Bosphorus cruise: a city ferry between Europe and Asia, paid with an İstanbulkart.
grand-bazaar: One of the world's oldest covered markets: 60+ streets of carpets, lamps, jewellery and leather. Closed on Sundays.
spice-bazaar: Spices, Turkish delight, dried fruit and tea next to the New Mosque in Eminönü.
balat: Colourful houses, churches, synagogues and cafés in the old Greek, Jewish and Armenian quarters on the Golden Horn.
istiklal: Istanbul's busiest street: shops, passages, churches and the red nostalgic tram, from Taksim to Galata.
ortakoy: The baroque Ortaköy Mosque under the Bosphorus Bridge, with street food like kumpir and waffles.
kadikoy: The lively Asian side: food market, cafés, bookshops and a seaside walk in Moda. Reach it by ferry.
camlica: The highest viewpoint on the Asian side and Turkey's largest mosque.
pierre-loti: Eyüp Sultan and Pierre Loti Hill
A holy mosque, then a short cable car up to a café with a view down the Golden Horn.
princes-islands: Car-free islands in the Sea of Marmara with wooden mansions and pine woods; a day trip by ferry.
emirgan: A large Bosphorus park with pavilions; famous for its tulips every April.

eminonu: Start at the New Mosque and the Spice Bazaar, then climb the busy market street of Rızapaşa Yokuşu.
suleymaniye: Mimar Sinan's mosque complex and the terrace above the Golden Horn.
kucukpazar: Walk down to the old market quarter with its wooden houses and craftsmen.
zeyrek: The Byzantine Pantokrator monastery (Zeyrek Mosque) and the Zeyrek Cistern.
carsamba: A conservative old neighbourhood around the Fethiye (Pammakaristos) Mosque.
balat: Colourful houses, the iron Bulgarian Church of St Stephen and the old synagogues.
ayvansaray: Where the land walls meet the Golden Horn: the Blachernae quarter and the Anemas dungeons.
edirnekapi: A gate of the Theodosian land walls and Sinan's Mihrimah Sultan Mosque.
yedikule: Follow the land walls south to the seven-towered fortress by the Golden Gate.
cerrahpasa: Turn back east through the old residential streets of the seventh hill.
beyazit: Beyazıt Square, the university gate, the Sahaflar book market and the Grand Bazaar.
sultanahmet: Finish at Hagia Sophia, the Blue Mosque and the Hippodrome.

jewish-heritage: Five centuries of Sephardic life: the old quarters of Balat and Hasköy, the Ahrida Synagogue, Galata and the Kamondo Stairs. Synagogue visits are arranged in advance with passport details.
armenian-heritage: Kumkapı and the Armenian Patriarchate with the Surp Asdvadzadzin church, the old quarter of Samatya and the Üç Horan church in Beyoğlu.
christian-istanbul: In the footsteps of early Christianity
Hagia Irene and Hagia Sophia, the mosaics of Chora, the Ecumenical Patriarchate at Fener, the iron Bulgarian church of St Stephen and the Pantokrator monastery.
ottoman-imperial: Topkapı Palace, the Süleymaniye and Rüstem Paşa mosques, the Grand Bazaar and the tiles of Sokollu Mehmed Paşa: the city of the sultans.
byzantine-ottoman: The Hippodrome, Hagia Sophia, the Basilica Cistern, the Blue Mosque, Topkapı Palace and the Grand Bazaar in one guided day.
golden-horn: Golden Horn: Fener, Balat and Eyüp
Colourful Balat and Fener, the Eyüp Sultan Mosque, the cable car up to Pierre Loti for the view, and back along the water.
uskudar: A ferry across the Bosphorus, the Mihrimah Sultan and Şemsi Paşa mosques, the Maiden's Tower from the shore and the view from Çamlıca Hill.
kadikoy-moda: Cross by ferry to the lively Asian side, taste your way through the Kadıköy market and walk along the sea in Moda.
beykoz: The green northern Bosphorus: Rumeli and Anadolu fortresses, the fishing village of Anadolu Kavağı, Yoros Castle and a fish lunch by the water.
panoramic-bus: An open-top bus past the main sights with audio commentary in several languages; hop off where you like and take a later bus. Good if you only have a day.
private-guide: A professional licensed guide just for your family or group, half or full day, on your own itinerary and in your language.
private-car: A car or minibus with a driver by the hour or the day, from a sedan for two to a minibus for large families. Combine it with a private guide.
vip-transfer: Airport or city transfers in a VIP van or luxury sedan, with meet and greet at arrivals.
anatolian-civilizations: Ankara's Museum of Anatolian Civilizations and Anıtkabir, the Hittite capital Hattusa, and the fairy chimneys of Cappadocia.
upper-mesopotamia: Gaziantep and the Zeugma mosaics, Şanlıurfa with Göbeklitepe and Balıklıgöl, the stone city of Mardin and sunrise on Mount Nemrut.

ui.routeCardText: 13 stops from Eminönü to Sultanahmet, through Süleymaniye, Balat, the land walls and Yedikule.
ui.rtLead: The historian İlber Ortaylı said you cannot claim to have seen Istanbul until you have walked it. This is the route he recommended, as reported in the Turkish press: from Eminönü up to Süleymaniye, through the old neighbourhoods to the land walls and Yedikule, and back to Sultanahmet.
ui.rtQuote: Don't say you have seen the city until you have walked these streets.
ui.rtQuoteBy: İlber Ortaylı, as quoted by the Turkish press
ui.rtTip1: Wear comfortable shoes: the streets are steep and often cobbled.
ui.rtTip2: Mosques: cover shoulders and knees, women cover their hair, and avoid prayer times.
ui.rtTip3: The walls between Edirnekapı and Yedikule are long and quiet; walk them in daylight or take a taxi for that part.
ui.rtDisclaimer: Bosphorly compiled this route from press reports of Prof. Ortaylı's recommendation. It is not an official route and is not endorsed by him or his family. Opening hours change; check before you go.
ui.rtMapNote: Straight lines between stops, not exact walking paths.

ui.gaSaw: M4 metro links Sabiha Gökçen Airport (SAW) on the Asian side with Kadıköy.
ui.gaTram: The T1 tram runs along the historic peninsula through Sultanahmet, Eminönü and Karaköy to Kabataş.
ui.gaFerry: City ferries cross between Europe and Asia. Pay for ferries, metro and trams with an İstanbulkart.
ui.gaNote: Lines and timetables change; check the official operators before you travel.
